clue.text: Character from 27 works in Spielberg film

definitions.meaning: The steel-toothed henchman in the James Bond films The Spy Who Loved Me and Moonraker

explanation.surface: A film buff spots a character from some well-known works appearing in a Spielberg movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the answer to 27-down, BOND; its 'works' are the James Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves a Bond henchman and the famous shark thriller, so both senses are titles or characters.

clue.text: How shoe may be repaired, outside very cracked

indicators.note: the repaired-shoe word sits outside, wrapping round the abbreviation for very

parts.note: a shoe is repaired by being soled, given a new sole

explanation.surface: A cobbler's note on mending a shoe that has a very bad crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' looks like damage to the shoe, but it is the definition: a puzzle cracked is solved.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or problem is to work it out, so cracked is a synonym of worked out.

clue.text: Character from 27 works readapting 27 works

indicators.note: works as a verb means is worked over or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: 27 points to the answer of 27-down, BOND

explanation.surface: Someone readapts a famous author's books, producing one of his characters.
explanation.walkthrough: The 27 here is Michael Bond, author of the Paddington books; 'works' is used twice, first as the author's books, then as the anagram signal for READAPTING plus BOND.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear, the marmalade-loving bear from Peru, is the creation of children's author Michael Bond.

clue.text: Believers back from America?

parts.note: hind means back or rear, as in hind legs
US is the abbreviation for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A question whether some believers have come back from America.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindus are followers of Hinduism, so they are believers in a religious faith.

clue.text: Qualified teacher strikes to get retirement cover

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the degree of a qualified teacher
socks means hits or strikes

explanation.surface: A qualified teacher goes on strike to secure cover for retirement, as if a pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedsocks are warm socks worn in bed, covering the feet when one retires for the night.

clue.text: Creator of 27 in toboggan, raising £1,000

indicators.note: in a down entry raising lifts the thousand symbol higher, so it moves to the front

parts.note: a luge is a racing toboggan
G, for grand, is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Someone on a toboggan raises a thousand pounds, perhaps for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 here is a bond in the sense of adhesion, not James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive sticks things together, so it creates a bond between them.

clue.text: Take back grappling iron left in a risky way

indicators.note: grappling means gripping, so the retracting word holds the other letters

parts.note: to unsay is to take back something said
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Instruction to take back a grappling iron that was left somewhere dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grappling iron' reads as one tool; 'grappling' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unsafely means doing it without regard to danger, hence riskily.

clue.text: 27 work about way to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: on means about, concerning
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A Bond film about a route heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr No (1962) was the first James Bond film, a work in the Bond franchise.

clue.text: Atomiser sprayed around a perfume

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the single letter a
sprayed means scattered, so the letters of atomiser are dispersed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An atomiser has sprayed a perfume about the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' puts A inside AROMTISE, the anagram of ATOMISER signalled by 'sprayed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To aromatise is to give a fragrance to something, so it is a verb sense of scent.

clue.text: Person opposed to 27 backing place for better learner

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the gambling city and learner are read in reverse

parts.note: Reno in Nevada is famous for its casinos, a place for a better (someone who bets)
L is the learner sign

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to Bond backs a better learner, like a rival spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 27 is just a bond, a union of people; 'better' is one who bets, not an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner shuns company and so avoids forming social ties with others.

clue.text: Day behind bar in 27 work

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the day letter is placed after the bar word

parts.note: bar and save both mean except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A day spent behind bars, as in a Bond film's prison scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places D after SAVE. The 27 work here is not a Bond film but Saved, the 1965 play by English playwright Edward Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Bond's controversial 1965 drama is titled Saved, so it is one of his plays.

clue.text: Criminal dares to get involved with dope

indicators.note: getting involved means mixing in together, so the two words' letters are combined and rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal is daring enough to get mixed up with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a bold lawbreaker of the Wild West kind.

clue.text: The man's receiving little knock in instances of corporal punishment

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the possessive word holds the knock

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
a ding is a slight dent or knock

explanation.surface: A man takes a small knock during an old-fashioned caning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidings are beatings, so each one is a physical chastisement.

clue.text: One who incarnated 27 English put in song

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the abbreviation for English goes into the song

parts.note: a hymn is a religious song

explanation.surface: An English actor who played Bond is put in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The bond here is marriage: Hymen was the Greek god of marriage, its embodiment, not an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hymen was the Greek deity of weddings, so he personified the marriage tie.

clue.text: One who incarnated 27 almost learnt lines

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is cut

parts.note: to con is to study or learn, so conned means learnt
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines

explanation.surface: An actor who played Bond almost learnt his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like an actor's script but means railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean Connery was the first actor to play James Bond on film, embodying the spy.

clue.text: I need clout, fooling around — it's in my DNA

indicators.note: fooling around means messing about, so the letters are played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they need clout, as fooling about is in their DNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids, so they are literally the units that make up genetic material.

clue.text: Not yet getting on with my interlocutor, nattering emptily

parts.note: the person I am speaking to is addressed as you

indicators.note: emptily means with the inside removed, so only the first and last letters of nattering stay

explanation.surface: Not getting on yet with the person you're chatting with, whose talk is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on means ageing, so someone not yet old is youthful.

clue.text: Sacred work is a tiny bit tacky at the outset

parts.note: a mote is a speck, a tiny bit

indicators.note: at the outset means at the start, so only the first letter of tacky is used

explanation.surface: A religious piece of music is judged a little tacky from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, usually on a religious text.

clue.text: Strategic opening of play in tense state

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the play's opening goes between tense and state

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
Cal is the abbreviation for California, a US state
Act I is the opening act of a play

explanation.surface: A strategic opening to a play set in an anxious place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense state' reads as anxiety; it is T and CAL. ACT I is Act One.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactical describes planning for advantage, closely related to strategic in everyday usage.

clue.text: Balletic movement not for Depardieu

definitions.meaning: French for not, and Gérard Depardieu is a French actor

explanation.surface: A ballet step that the burly French actor will not attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a ballet step and also the French negative used with ne.

clue.text: Rules of behaviour for officer to keep to

indicators.note: to keep means to hold, so the support word and officer hold the little word between them

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer is given rules of behaviour to keep to.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'to' is the signal 'to keep'; the second is the piece held, a common trick of reusing a short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the code of etiquette or correct procedure in official settings.

clue.text: Showing false modesty, leading around rodent

parts.note: coy means affectedly shy or modest

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for leading is reversed

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: A coy creature, ahead in some race, looks round.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: Bob carries jug round? Impossible!

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the bob word holds the jug

parts.note: to bob the head is to nod
a can is a vessel, a jug
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Bob is asked to carry a jug round and refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but means a nod.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal refusal saying something cannot be done.

clue.text: This person, about to stop affair, is creator of 27

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the reversed pronoun is placed inside the affair

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pronoun is reversed

parts.note: this person, the writer, is me

explanation.surface: Someone about to end an affair turns out to be the creator of Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming wrote the James Bond novels, so he invented the spy.

clue.text: See 25
1 and 8 shot, including a hostile attack

parts.note: the numeral one is the Roman I

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the scrambled film title holds the letter a
shot means wrecked or damaged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 8 points to the answer of 8-down, DR NO

explanation.surface: Bond films 1 and 8 were shot, including a hostile attack.
explanation.walkthrough: '1' looks like 1-down; it is just I. 'Including' puts A inside NROD, the anagram of DRNO from 'shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is a raid or incursion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Make blue colour hems in Gerald's jacket

indicators.note: hems in means encloses, so the colour surrounds the other letters

parts.note: brown is a colour

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside, so the first and last letters of the name are used

explanation.surface: Someone wants to make Gerald's jacket blue by dyeing the hems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is not a colour here but low spirits, and the jacket is the outside of the name Gerald, ignoring the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring someone down is to depress them, and blue means sad.

clue.text: See 3
Person opposed to 27 shot after part of target

indicators.note: after means following, so the drink measure comes after the target part

parts.note: the gold is the bullseye ring at the centre of an archery target
a finger is a measure of spirits, as is a shot

explanation.surface: A villain takes a shot at part of a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like firing at the target but is a drink measure; the gold is the bullseye of an archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric Goldfinger is the villain of the 1959 Fleming novel and 1964 film, Bond's adversary.

clue.text: Pulse in broth that needs stirring

indicators.note: stirring mixes the contents, so the letters of broth are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pulses, as lentils, go into a broth that needs stirring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests lentils for the soup; it means a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong rhythmic beat, like a heartbeat.

clue.text: English playwright sure to leave university

indicators.note: to leave means to depart, so the university letter is removed

parts.note: bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: An English playwright is certain to leave university.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Bond is an English dramatist, author of Saved and Lear.

clue.text: A bridal accessory said to provide help

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is read for its sound

parts.note: a veil is worn by a bride

explanation.surface: A bridal accessory is said to be helpful at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or benefit, an old verb for being helpful.

clue.text: Like some accounts with exaggerated depiction

definitions.meaning: an ... bank account has had more taken out than was in it
drawn or described in an exaggerated way

explanation.surface: Accounts with an exaggerated depiction, like an inflated story.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a bank balance in debit and a portrayal drawn too heavily.
